shots.vo: They brought home a smart fridge that ordered groceries before they ever ran out.
It learned everything. Dad's protein shakes.
Mom's oat milk. The kids' chocolate pudding.
It was never wrong.
Then one Sunday, the weekly delivery showed up.
Oat milk. Pudding. But no protein shakes.
He laughed it off as a glitch and reordered them himself.
The next week, they were gone again.
You see, the fridge didn't just track what they ate.
It listened. It watched. It predicted.
And now, it was only ordering food for three.
He started to panic. He checked the brakes on his car.
He stopped driving at night. He even had his heart checked. Perfectly healthy.
His wife told him he was being ridiculous.
She kissed his forehead and promised him nothing was going to happen.
That night, he couldn't sleep, so he opened the fridge's order history.
Every item had been predicted by the AI. Except one.
It had been added by hand, from his wife's account.
A box of rat poison. They didn't have rats.
He turned around. She was standing in the kitchen doorway, holding his favorite dinner.
